summary: The Mathematical and Statistical Modeling Education Act directs the National Science Foundation to coordinate research and development efforts aimed at modernizing mathematics and statistics in pre-kindergarten through 12th-grade education. It focuses on incorporating mathematical and statistical modeling, data science, computational thinking, and project-based learning into schools through competitive awards, partnerships, and an independent study by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine.

affected_groups.effect: Gain increased access to modern mathematics and statistics curricula, real-world data analysis, and problem-based learning approaches.
Receive professional learning opportunities, training resources, and hands-on research experiences to integrate modeling and data science into teaching.
Are eligible to apply for competitive federal awards and grants to research and advance innovative educational approaches.
affected_groups.group: Institutions of Higher Education and Nonprofits

key_provisions: Directs the National Science Foundation Director to award competitive, merit-reviewed grants to higher education institutions, nonprofits, or consortia for research and development in mathematical modeling education.
Requires grant applicants to describe target populations, including historically underrepresented groups in STEM, students experiencing homelessness, and youth in foster care.
Authorizes funds to be used for educator professional development, curriculum research, real-world data analysis tools, and building partnerships between schools and employers.
Requires the National Science Foundation to evaluate the funded programs, share best practices, and report findings to Congress.

Directs an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) to conduct a study and public meeting on the implementation and barriers of mathematical and statistical modeling in K-12 education.

Authorizes $10,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the National Science Foundation Directorate for STEM Education to carry out the grant program, and $1,000,000 annually for the NASEM study.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Mathematical and Statistical Modeling Education Act directs the National Science Foundation to coordinate research and development efforts aimed at modernizing mathematics and statistics in pre-kindergarten through 12th-grade education. It focuses on incorporating mathematical and statistical modeling, data science, computational thinking, and project-based learning into schools through competitive awards, partnerships, and an independent study by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes federal grant programs and national studies aimed at updating school mathematics and statistics instruction to align with modern workforce needs in data science, artificial intelligence, and related STEM fields. It authorizes specific funding levels totaling several million dollars annually through fiscal year 2030.
